about: Position-NFT permit vectors — Uniswap v3 NonfungiblePositionManager and v4 PositionManager. Inputs only; expectations are derived by verify_nft_ours.py --emit and cross-checked by verify_nft_sdk.mjs.
note_integers: Every integer is a decimal string, for the reason recorded in ../vectors/README.md: JSON numbers are IEEE-754 doubles in JavaScript.
note_the_trap: v3 and v4 share the struct type hash 0x49ecf333... and differ only in the domain: v3 has a `version` field, v4 does not. Checking the type hash therefore proves nothing about which contract will accept the signature.
note_onchain: Each case pins the domain separator reported by the deployed contract on 2026-08-15. verify_nft_ours.py recomputes it offline and compares — so the file fails if either our reading or the chain moves.

cases.why: The exact shape the UniversalRouter forwards under command 0x11 (V3_POSITION_MANAGER_PERMIT): approve the router for one position so it can migrate it. Four-field domain, with version.
Same message on Base. Only chainId and verifyingContract move, and the digest is unrecognisably different.

The v3 nonce is per tokenId and lives on chain (_positions[tokenId].nonce++). The signer must read it before signing and cannot verify it locally — this case exists so the encoding of a non-zero nonce is pinned.

🔴 The trap, made explicit. Byte-for-byte the same struct as the first case — same type hash, same spender, same tokenId, same nonce, same deadline — and a completely different digest, because the v4 domain has no `version`. Nothing in the type hash warns you.
v4 on Base. The nonce here is an unordered bitmap keyed by OWNER, not by tokenId — a different scheme from v3 with the same field name.

🔴 The unbounded approval of the position path. No tokenId, no amount, no ceiling: `approved = true` hands one address control of every position the owner holds, present and future. Permit2 at least has an amount field to cap; this one has nothing but the deadline. Policy refuses it outside a narrow allow-list.

The same message with approved = false REVOKES. A policy that refuses PermitForAll wholesale would block the owner from withdrawing an operator's blanket access — refusing a revocation is the mirror of the expiration=0 mistake in the Permit2 set.
